title: useArrayBoundarySeparator ON: index-like keys and an array of objects
rationale: The required flag-ON arm, and the vehicle for a correction: the flag does NOT mark array boundaries. getSeparator() returns "__" and both array branches compute the identical expression. The flag is a global separator rename with no array-boundary semantics - the repo signature pathology in the exact control the brief asked to exercise. Index-like map keys guard against a future reconstructor reading them as array indices.
catchesBugClass: Round-trip correctness under the alternate separator, including that FlattenedPath escapes the separator FIRST character so multi-character separators do not mis-split, and that numeric map keys stay object keys.
cannotCatch: It cannot catch the thing the flag NAME promises, because that behaviour does not exist to break. It also silently depends on the caller reconfiguring the reconstructor separator; nothing in the flattened output declares which separator produced it.

predicted.detail: Semantically identical to the flag-OFF run - only the character count of the keys differs.
